extracted.intended_audience: U.S. patent examiners and patent practitioners (applicants/attorneys/agents)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedures and substantive requirements for requesting or issuing suspensions/deferrals of Office action, and rules for periods for reply, extensions, and abandonment in U.S. patent prosecution (37 CFR 1.103, 1.135, 1.136, related MPEP guidance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition for suspension under 37 CFR 1.103(a)
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition for suspension of action under 37 CFR 1.103(a) must be presented as a separate paper; be accompanied by the petition fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(g); request a specific and reasonable period of suspension not greater than 6 months; and present good and sufficient reasons why the suspension is necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If requirements of 1.103(a) are met, the Office may grant suspension for the specified period (begins on filing day). If not met, expect application to be taken up for action. Use prescribed form paragraphs ¶ 7.54 (grant) and ¶ 7.56 (dismissal). Only TC Director can grant second or subsequent suspensions; such approval must appear on Office letter. A supplemental reply filed during suspension will be entered (see MPEP § 714.03(a)).

rubrics_metrics.name: What constitutes 'good and sufficient cause' for 1.103(a)
rubrics_metrics.description: The showing must specifically explain what factors directly impact the applicant’s ability to presently prosecute the application; a general statement (e.g., global pandemic) may not suffice without specific explanation of impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-limiting examples where good and sufficient cause may be found: (A) inventor suffering poor health or unavailable due to factors beyond control (e.g., active military overseas); (B) application subject to litigation impacting prosecution (ownership/assignment dispute); (C) applicant needs more time to prepare data requested by examiner or to support a declaration to supplement a response. Situations where requests may be dismissed as lacking good and sufficient cause: (A) applicant needs more time to determine prosecution strategy; (B) financial hardship; (C) still developing business strategy; filing an IDS to allow time is dismissed because 37 CFR 1.97 provides recourse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for suspension with CPA or RCE under 37 CFR 1.103(b) or (c)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants may request suspension of action under 1.103(b) or (c) for a period not exceeding three months when filed at the time of filing a CPA (continued prosecution application) or an RCE (request for continued examination).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirements: (A) request must be filed with the filing of a design CPA or an RCE (use transmittal form check box or separate paper); (1) if with an RCE, the RCE must comply with 1.114 (submission and fee 1.17(e)) — payment of the RCE fee may not be deferred and request cannot substitute for the submission; (2) if with a CPA, a filing date must be assigned to the CPA; (B) request should specify period in whole months (max 3) — if none specified or exceeds 3 months, Office will assume 3 months; (C) request must include processing fee 1.17(i). Missing parts for CPA: if filing date assigned, suspension processed even if CPA fees missing; applicant given 2 months to pay CPA basic filing fee, search fee, examination fee and surcharge to avoid abandonment. Improper CPA/RCE (no filing date, RCE without submission or fee): Office will not recognize suspension request and time in prior communications continues to run. If request improper (untimely or without processing fee), action not suspended and CPA/RCE processed; examiner to notify applicant using form ¶ 7.56.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deferral of examination under 37 CFR 1.103(d) (applicant request)
rubrics_metrics.description: On request, Office may grant deferral of examination under 1.103(d) for a period not extending beyond three years from the earliest filing date for which a benefit is claimed; request must include the publication fee 1.18(d) and processing fee 1.17(i).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A request for deferral will not be granted unless: (1) application is an original utility or plant application filed under 1.53(b) or results from entry of an international application into national stage after compliance with 1.495 (cannot be design, reissue, or CPA under 1.53(d)); (2) application filed on or after Nov 29, 2000; (3) applicant has not filed a nonpublication request under 1.213(a), or if filed must rescind under 1.213(b); (4) application is in condition for publication as provided in 1.211(c); and (5) Office has not issued an Office action under 35 U.S.C. 132 or a notice of allowance under 35 U.S.C. 151. If request missing or exceeds max period, Office will assume maximum requested. A supervisory patent examiner’s approval (TC level) is required to grant deferral. Use form ¶ 7.54.01 (granted) or ¶ 7.56.02 (denied).

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of applicant-requested suspension/deferral on patent term adjustment
rubrics_metrics.description: Suspension of action under 37 CFR 1.103(a)-(d) at the applicant’s request will cause a reduction in patent term adjustment (PTA) accumulated under 37 CFR 1.703.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The reduction equals the number of days beginning on the date a request for suspension was filed and ending on the date of termination of the suspension. See 37 CFR 1.704(c)(1) for computation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improper request consequences and processing when suspension request is improper
rubrics_metrics.description: If the request for suspension is improper (e.g., untimely, without requisite processing fee, improper CPA/RCE), the Office will not suspend action; the CPA or RCE will be processed and the application placed on the examiner’s docket.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner will notify applicant of denial in the next Office communication (use form ¶ 7.56.01 or ¶ 7.56.02). If CPA assigned a filing date but missing fees, applicant will have 2 months to pay or CPA abandoned; suspension acts only to suspend first Office action but does not affect missing part processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Termination of suspension of action
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for termination of a suspension of action will be effective when an appropriate official of the Office takes action thereon; if the request properly identifies the application and the suspension period has not expired when the Office acts, the Office will terminate the suspension and place the application on the examiner’s docket.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An acknowledgment should be sent to applicant using form ¶ 7.54.02 (termination granted).

rubrics_metrics.name: Office-initiated suspension of action (37 CFR 1.103(e) and (f))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office may suspend action on its own initiative and will notify applicant; such suspensions are limited to a maximum period of 6 months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners may grant an initial suspension (max 6 months) for reasons like awaiting a reference or possible interference (use form ¶ 7.52 or ¶ 7.53). Second or subsequent suspensions require Technology Center (TC) Director approval and the Director’s signature must appear on the letter. Suspension under 1.103(f) is decided by the TC Director who oversees Licensing and Review. Office-initiated suspensions should be avoided if possible and must be terminated once the reason no longer exists. Guidance to update search or find alternate sources if reference remains unavailable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph use and examiner notes for suspension actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific form paragraphs are provided for notifying applicants of grant/denial of suspension/deferral and for inspector use (e.g., ¶ 7.54, ¶ 7.54.01, ¶ 7.54.02, ¶ 7.56, ¶ 7.56.01, ¶ 7.56.02, ¶ 7.52, ¶ 7.53).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner notes clarify maximum periods, approval authorities (TC Director for second/subsequent suspensions), and bracket insertions for dates and reasons. Use these standardized paragraphs in Office communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overlapping applications by same applicant or same assignee
rubrics_metrics.description: In general, examiners should not consider ex parte questions which are pending before the Office in inter partes proceedings involving the same applicant when at least one application/patent of the same applicant involved in interference/derivation/inter partes proceedings contains claims that overlap with claims of the application under examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When such a situation arises, the examiner should consult with the Technology Center Quality Assurance Specialist to determine appropriate course of action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory period for reply and abandonment (35 U.S.C. 133; 37 CFR 1.135)
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicant fails to prosecute the application within six months after any action therein (or within such shorter time not less than thirty days fixed by the Director), the application shall be regarded as abandoned. 37 CFR 1.135 provides that failure to reply within the time set in 1.134 and 1.136 will result in abandonment unless an Office action indicates otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.135(b): admission of, or refusal to admit, any amendment after final rejection or any amendment not responsive to the last action will not operate to save the application from abandonment. Where a reply is a bona fide attempt to advance the application but is substantially complete except for an inadvertent omission, examiner may give a new shortened statutory time (generally 2 months) to supply omission (see MPEP § 710.01 and § 714.03(a)). Examiner discretion applies to whether omission precludes action on merits or can be waived.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of bona fide attempts to reply with inadvertent omissions (37 CFR 1.135(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: When a bona fide attempt to reply includes an inadvertent omission that precludes action on the merits (e.g., unsigned or improperly signed amendment, amendment requiring additional fees not paid), the examiner may treat the reply adequate to avoid abandonment and give applicant a shortened statutory time period (generally 2 months) to correct the omission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to timely supply the omission will result in abandonment. If the omission does not preclude action on the merits (e.g., reply fails to address a rejection), the examiner may waive the deficiency and act on the application or issue an action that either does not treat the reply on merits but requires supply of omission or that does treat the reply on merits and may require supply of omission. Providing the 2-month period is discretionary. Where omission not inadvertent (abuse to gain time), examiner should notify applicant and require supply within the period for reply to the prior action (including permitted extensions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Computation of statutory and shortened reply periods
rubrics_metrics.description: Actual time for reply is computed from the notification or mail date printed on the Office action to the date of receipt by the Office of applicant’s reply; no fractions of a day are taken into account and reply is due on the corresponding day of the month N months after the Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples given: reply to an Office action with a 3-month shortened statutory period dated November 30 is due Feb 28 (or 29 leap year); reply to Office action dated Feb 28 is due May 28. A 1-month extension moves due date to corresponding day next month (example Jan 31 with 3-month period => Apr 30; one-month extension => May 31). When a timely reply is not filed, the application is abandoned after midnight of the date the period expired. A 30-day period includes Saturdays, Sundays, and federal holidays, but if period ends on weekend/holiday reply timely if filed next succeeding business day. Date of receipt recorded in electronic file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensions of time under 37 CFR 1.136 (shortened statutory periods and other extensions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 37 CFR 1.136(a), if applicant is required to reply within a nonstatutory or shortened statutory time period, applicant may extend the time up to the earlier of the maximum period set by statute or five months after the time set for reply if a petition and fee under 1.17(a) are filed, unless exclusions apply. The petition filing date is the date used to determine the extension period and corresponding fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions where paragraph (a) extension not available: (i) applicant notified otherwise in Office action; (ii) reply is a reply brief under 41.41; (iii) reply is request for oral hearing under 41.47(a); (iv) reply to Patent Trial and Appeal Board decisions per specified sections; (v) application involved in contested case or derivation proceeding. Constructive petition: a written authorization to treat any concurrent or future reply requiring a petition and fee as incorporating a petition for extension will be treated as a constructive petition; authorization to charge fees will also be treated as constructive petition. Under 1.136(b), when paragraph (a) not available, extension will be granted only for sufficient cause for a reasonable time, filed on or before due date with petition fee 1.17(g), and cannot extend beyond the statutory maximum. Under 1.136(c), certain time periods set in a Notice of Allowability are not extendable (periods for submitting inventor’s oath/declaration, formal drawings per 1.85(c), and deposits per 1.809(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping and docketing rules related to suspension and reply periods
rubrics_metrics.description: When suspension is granted, the application will be placed in suspension status until end of suspension; upon expiration it will be placed on the examiner’s docket for further prosecution. The date of receipt of a reply is recorded in the electronic file as the receipt date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If suspension is granted but supplemental reply filed within suspension, it will be entered (see MPEP § 714.03(a)). Examiners should docket actions upon termination or expiration of suspension and update search or find alternatives when awaiting references. Failure to process proper CPA/RCE or missing fees has specific docketing consequences as described above.
